pairs.reason: Impl 1's shared _Table/_highlights model means a new format only lays out tables, while Impl 2 repeats headings, column lists and row comprehensions in every renderer. Impl 1 is heavier and adds row validation that wasn't asked for, but its tests are much more thorough: exact empty output for all formats, ties, short rows, and rejection before the file is read.

Impl 1 is a lean, well-sized single-file refactor, while Impl 2 splits into three modules and adds CSV validation, which goes beyond the task. Even so, Impl 2's tests pin the byte-identical edge cases (empty input in every format, summation order, -0.00, ties, rejecting a bad format before reading), which Impl 1 barely covers.

Impl 1 stays in one file and its generic ReportContent makes adding formats easy, though Column.text_width lets text layout leak into the supposedly neutral model. Impl 2 is clean but spreads the change over three modules with verbose, repetitive tests, so the two are close.
